blocks.source: Vol IV, The Nervous System, § Chunk Lease Sizing from the Stopping Budget
blocks.md: A learned policy runtime can stall for many reasons: a page fault, thermal throttling on the vision accelerator, memory fragmentation, or an uncaught exception in perception preprocessing. The robot does not stop when its software does. A loaded base keeps its momentum (LinearMomentum = Mass SpeedAtDetection) and covers … every millisecond at the drive limit, while the downstream controller keeps converting the remaining waypoints of the last admitted chunk into setpoints.

questions.q: The section **Chunk Lease Sizing from the Stopping Budget** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Under any workload the proposer can generate, the permission path must meet its response bound and keep its authority to refuse, and separate processors are one realization of that requirement, a hypothesis that loaded tests must still confirm.

An admitted chunk may drive the actuators only for a lease counted on the permission path's own clock, derived from the plant: longer than the renewal period plus jitter and short enough to fit under the pre-brake ceiling of the stopping budget.

Proposals cross rate boundaries as state messages, not events, so a single-slot seqlock or wait-free multi-slot mailbox gives the faster reader one bounded, nonblocking attempt per tick that returns a complete snapshot or keeps the previous one.

Each tier takes its rate from a different physical constant (winding L/R and the PWM carrier for the current loop, base travel per tick for the permission tick, weight-sweep cost for the chunk policy, prefill cost for the intent model), not from convenience.
